title: Inspect and extend: Test routing, tab lifecycle, and privacy claims
objective: Use the real implementation in `Tests/BrowserCoreTests.swift` to demonstrate and safely improve xctest coverage, xcodegen project configuration, and documentation boundary.
problem: Tests are executable examples of expected browser rules. Compare each claim to source and tests, then identify runtime checks for navigation, persistence, and content rules. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `Tests/BrowserCoreTests.swift` and the related project files: Tests/BrowserCoreTests.swift; project.yml; README.md.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to xctest coverage, xcodegen project configuration, and documentation boundary.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: No Xcode build was run in this workspace; simulator behavior remains unverified.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: Tests are executable examples of expected browser rules. Compare each claim to source and tests, then identify runtime checks for navigation, persistence, and content rules.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `Tests/BrowserCoreTests.swift`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
